messages.subject: Multiple likelihoods with different scales/variances
parts:
I'm looking at using INLA to fit a model for likelihoods with different known variances, similar to the example at http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools#TOC-Models-with-more-than-one-type-of-likelihood

Currently the results I get for the marginal distribution of the fixed effect are different to my other numerical method, so my first question is: Does INLA fit the model that I want?

L(p; x1, s1*v1) L(p; x2, s2*v2) ... L(p; xn, sn*vn)
where
v1 ~ F(t)
v2 ~ F(t)
...
vn ~ F(t)
and the s1,..,sn are known and fixed.

I want to know the marginal distribution of p.

I fit this as something like

X <- matrix(NA, 5, 5)
diag(X) <- c(1,2,2.5,3,3.7)

g <- inla(X ~ 1,
          family=rep("gaussian",5),
          data = list(X=X),
          scale = c(2,3,5,4,2),
          control.family = list(
            list(hyper=list(theta=list("logtnormal", c(0,1)))),
            list(hyper=list(theta=list("logtnormal", c(0,1)))),
            list(hyper=list(theta=list("logtnormal", c(0,1)))),
            list(hyper=list(theta=list("logtnormal", c(0,1)))),
            list(hyper=list(theta=list("logtnormal", c(0,1))))
          ))

and look at g$fixed.marginal$intercept.

Thanks
Joe S.
